text.p: These are the leading storied in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Minimum expenses for a four member family for food, clothing and utilities stood at 2,118 dinars ($424) in October according to the federal statistics office. Cost of food alone went up by 7.3 percent in October on the previous month, it said.

- Serbian furniture factory Simpo's products are of high quality and can compete with the best furniture producing countries such as Italy and Germany. Its exports to Germany alone expected to reach $20 million in 1997, says company president and Serbian minister coordinator Dragan Tomic.
- The Bosnian Serb Army will continue its reorganisation and professionalisation, says the newly appointed commander General Pero Colic in Pale.
- Claims that Bosnian Serb leaders Ratko Mladic and Radovan Karadzic will take refuge in the Chyllandar monastery in Greece are provocations and have no approval from Greek authorities, commentary.
- Interest on credits extended by commercial banks to the economy are between 8 and 15 ercent a month.
- The new federal Yugoslav government will probably be elected by the end of the year.

- Deputy Speaker of the Yugoslav parliament Radmilo Bogdanovic says the new parlaiment will be able to operate normally and make decisions without obstruction with the number of deputies of left parties elected at the November 3 elections.

- Belgrade's telecommunications firm Pupin Telecom proposes new telephone convertor which will lower costs of opening new telephone lines. It is entering into competition with foreign producers of the same equipment.
